title: US Measles Cases Pass 6,000 in 2026 as CDC Counts Nine Deaths
excerpt: The CDC counted 6,039 confirmed cases as of November 24 — more than the whole of 2025 — with 97% of cases tied to outbreaks across 47 jurisdictions.
body:
• The United States has recorded 6,039 confirmed measles cases in 2026 as of November 24, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — already more than the 2,289 cases reported in all of 2025.
  • The CDC counts nine measles deaths in 2026 so far, a figure it says is subject to change; its previous update, as of November 19, counted 5,838 cases and reported two more deaths, in Wisconsin and Pennsylvania.
  • Of this year's confirmed cases, 97% are outbreak-associated, and cases have been reported by 47 jurisdictions, with 18 cases among international visitors to the US.
  • For families in the US, the practical step is to confirm every household member's MMR vaccination status — the CDC's measles page carries the current case counts and guidance.

The United States' measles outbreak has passed 6,000 confirmed cases. As of November 24, 2026, 6,039 confirmed measles cases were reported in the United States in 2026, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Of those, 6,021 cases were reported by 47 jurisdictions, and 18 cases were reported among international visitors to the United States.

For the full year of 2025, a total of 2,289 confirmed cases were reported in the United States. The 2026 count has passed that full-year total with more than a month of the year still to run.

Deaths, and why the counts differ

The CDC's deaths table lists nine measles deaths in the United States in 2026, and notes the number is subject to change as reviews are completed. The agency is working with the Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists to develop a standardized case definition for deaths due to measles, which is one reason state and federal tallies have not always matched.

In its previous weekly update, the CDC counted 5,838 confirmed cases as of November 19, Reuters reported, as the country battled its worst outbreak of the viral infection in decades. That update followed two more reported deaths, in Wisconsin and Pennsylvania. Pennsylvania, the hardest-hit state in that report, had confirmed 1,631 measles cases including 326 hospitalizations as of November 20, and Wisconsin had reported two deaths.

An outbreak-driven year

There have been 43 new outbreaks reported in 2026, and 97% of confirmed cases — 5,829 of 6,039 — are outbreak-associated: 4,444 from outbreaks that started in 2026 and 1,385 from outbreaks that started in 2025. In 2025, by comparison, 48 outbreaks were reported and 90% of confirmed cases were outbreak-associated.

The CDC notes that it is aware of probable measles cases being reported by jurisdictions, but its page includes only confirmed cases that jurisdictions have notified to the agency. It also cautions that the 2025 and 2026 case counts are preliminary and subject to change. The agency's cases page was updated on November 25, 2026; because of a federal holiday, the next data update is scheduled for December 4, 2026.

What readers should do

Measles spreads through outbreaks in under-vaccinated communities, and the CDC's figures show nearly every case this year is tied to an outbreak. Families can check the CDC measles page for the latest state-by-state picture and vaccination guidance, and confirm their children's MMR doses are up to date before holiday travel.
